chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

All clay is unlawful, like the flesh of a swine. And whoever eats it and then dies from it, I will not pray over him, except the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it contains a cure for every disease. And whoever eats it with craving, there will not be a cure in it.

key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Clay of the grave of al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating clay and is the clay of Imam Husayn's grave an exception?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) declaring all clay haram akin to pork, with the sole exception of the soil from Imam al-Husayn’s grave, which possesses curative properties for physical ailments. This exception is conditional upon being consumed with intentionality rather than mere gluttony, highlighting the spiritual potency of the Imam’s resting place. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the metaphysical healing power (shifa) inherent in the graves of the Ahl al-Bayt.
